title: Halloween at Ten Coaster Parks: Every Event Compared
h1: Halloween at every park on this site: nine events, one honest ranking of what each is for
description: Every Halloween event at the ten parks this site covers — Knott's Scary Farm, three Howl-O-Screams, four Fright Fests and Legoland's Brick-or-Treat — compared by intensity, cost and audience.
summary: Halloween at these ten parks is nine different products for four different audiences: two hard-ticket haunt tiers, four included overlays, and one deliberate anti-haunt for young families. This is the map.
typicalWindow: Mid-September through Halloween night, parks running weekends-first calendars

sections.heading: The three tiers of scare
body: The hard-ticket haunts — Knott's Scary Farm and the three Howl-O-Screams — are produced evening events with haunted houses, scare actors and coasters after dark, sold as separate tickets. The included overlays — the four Six Flags Fright Fests — are atmosphere layered on a normal ride day, free with admission. And the deliberate counterweight — Legoland's Brick-or-Treat — is Halloween with the fear removed, for the under-tens.
Choosing between tiers is choosing the evening's product, not its quality: a haunt fan's best night is a family's worst, and this site ranks them within their purpose rather than across it.

sections.heading: The intensity ladder, plainly
body: For scare tolerance, the honest order from most to least intense: Knott's Scary Farm first — the genre's founder and still its benchmark — then the Howl-O-Screams at Orlando, San Antonio and San Diego in a tight band, then the Fright Fests as a clear step down in production and intensity, and Brick-or-Treat last with none at all.

Age guidance follows the same ladder: the hard-ticket events recommend against young guests in their own materials, Fright Fest evenings are PG-13 with roaming actors, and Brick-or-Treat is built precisely for the kids every other line excludes.

sections.heading: The planning calendar
body: Everything opens in the last ten days of September and runs weekends through Halloween. The crowd physics are uniform across all nine: opening-weekend and weeknight dates run calm, the last two Saturdays before Halloween run at the year's peak, and the best dates sell out first at every hard-ticket event.

Buy haunt tickets early and buy the calm nights; show up to Fright Fests whenever because they are included; and take the young family to Brick-or-Treat on whichever weekend fits, because its crowds are the gentlest of the season.

southern-california.verdict: The deepest Halloween region on this site: the flagship haunt, a strong SeaWorld haunt, the biggest Fright Fest and the family event, all within two hours.
southern-california.note: Knott's Scary Farm is the region's — arguably the country's — anchor event; Brick-or-Treat covers the young-family case the same weekends.

texas.verdict: Two solid options: the Arlington Fright Fest on day admission and San Antonio's Howl-O-Scream as the produced night event.
texas.note: The Texas haunts pair naturally with the fall weather window — October is the civilised month to be outdoors in both markets.

orlando.verdict: Howl-O-Scream is the value play in the Halloween capital — the same produced-haunt ambition as the resort events, usually cheaper, with better coasters running after dark.
orlando.note: Orlando's Halloween season is a three-way contest with the Disney and Universal events; the SeaWorld haunt is the coaster fan's pick of the three.

new-jersey.verdict: One event, and a big one: Great Adventure's Fright Fest Saturdays are the Northeast's biggest fall theme-park nights.
new-jersey.note: The peak Saturdays here are among the year's biggest crowds at any park on this site — the line-skip guide's haunt-season advice applies doubled.

chicago.verdict: Great America's Fright Fest is the region's default Halloween park night, with the lake wind as its signature special effect.
chicago.note: The October weekends here have the best atmosphere-to-crowd ratio of the four Fright Fests — the park's seasonal calendar is the region's most complete.

faqs.q: Which Halloween event is the best on this site?
faqs.a: Knott's Scary Farm, for haunt fans — it is the oldest big haunt in the country and still the benchmark for maze count and atmosphere. For value, the weeknight Howl-O-Scream tickets usually undercut the resort-park events while keeping the produced-haunt ambition.

faqs.q: Which is best for young kids?
faqs.a: Brick-or-Treat at Legoland California, unconditionally — it is the only event on this site with zero scare content. The Fright Fest daytime hours are the second answer: the overlays do not fully staff until dusk.

faqs.q: Are the haunts worth the separate tickets?
faqs.a: The hard-ticket events deliver a categorically different product from the included overlays — real haunted houses and produced nights against decorated ride days. If scares are the goal, yes; if riding is the goal, a Fright Fest weekend or any weekday serves better.

faqs.q: When do the events announce their dates?
faqs.a: Typically late August into early September, with Knott's usually earliest. This site carries every event as a pattern with a confidence label until the parks publish the current cycle's dates.

freshness.sourceNote: Event structure, windows and audience descriptions are multi-year patterns across the nine events; no 2026 dates, lineups or prices have been verified by this site as of 2026-07. Each event's own page carries its specific confidence and source note.
